answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card simultaneously; add one per fatigue and +1 for Chairman. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move retiree to Pensioners, flip the card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.

evidence.quote: Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard a display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties go to most total windows (including new prizes), then clockwise from PM. The actor may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace a card during selection; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players. Then discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if no one took one; return all unused Pensioners to supplies.

evidence.quote: Players who retired at least one pensioner must each take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties: most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM.

answers.answer: At Family phase start check the opportunity marker; choose a main action once, or twice if the marker already matched it; move the marker to the chosen action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action, which is not doubled and does not move the marker. Enlist Writer places one extra writer once this turn if at least four offices are vacant; with a doubled Writer action and four vacancies, three writers total can be placed.

evidence.quote: Choose a main family action: take it once, or may take it twice if the marker already matched it. Place/move the opportunity marker onto your chosen main action.

answers.answer: After family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one, repeating. When Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. Seek Share purchase money was paid to the bank at application; it is not paid into Company treasuries.

evidence.summary_location: Turn Structure / Family — New Company shares
evidence.quote: After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one. Repeat while both remain. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order.

answers.answer: Fill vacancies by ascending number on card backs. Ordinary own-family hiring requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman election and Commander appointments are exempt. On promotion, transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, vacant, in ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

evidence.summary_location: Hiring — general rules and Nepotism table
evidence.quote: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card.

answers.answer: Former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody gets support, former Chairman picks any shareholder, including self. No Nepotism applies. The winner’s Company share moves into Chairman slot and remains a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.

evidence.quote: Move one winner’s Company shares into Chairman slot and give title marker. It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.

answers.answer: Commit resources/cash first; check cash comes from the acting office treasury and is paid to bank. Gather dice and subtract penalties; use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office limits allow; 5–6 catastrophe, no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue and flip card to Vacant Offices. Commander/firm procedures may modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success.

evidence.quote: First commit resources/cash: all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll. Use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 catastrophic failure

answers.answer: Chairman may borrow up to three Debt freely, receiving £5 Balance per Debt. Every further advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts). Never advance past the Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting borrowing limits. Existing office cash remains there.

evidence.quote: May add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling majority Company shares (Chairman counts); never pass Debt track end.

answers.answer: Manager of Shipping must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. Lease extra ship £2; fit a ship from a shipyard £3 without owner consent; buy a Company ship £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each in any sea zone, including China once it exists; extra ships last until Refresh.

evidence.quote: Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. Lease extra ship £2; fit ship from shipyard £3 without owner consent; buy Company ship £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards.

answers.answer: Declare home region plus only regions reachable through open orders and available ship capacity. Each £1 of President treasury buys a die; subtract one per declared nonhome region. On success, capacity is one order per ship in that Presidency sea zone; ships do not exhaust. Fill home first, then extend only the route filled in this Trade (writers from other Presidencies cannot extend it); use all writers then filled tokens for remaining ships. Cannot fill another Presidency’s home even if its office is vacant. One successful Trade per President per turn. President gets £1/order from bank; each placed writer’s owner gets £1; Company Balance rises by full printed value or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn.

evidence.quote: Declare regions for Trade: include home region, and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one per declared nonhome region.

answers.answer: Commander may target own Presidency home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region; not another home or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company target must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for printed dice; subtract target and all other regions in its empire (target once), but Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted; each 6 returns that officer to supply; regiments do not roll officer-loss dice.

evidence.quote: Target own Presidency’s home, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. Cannot target another home region or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region.

answers.answer: On success loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, minimum surviving participating officers in that attempt +1 (Commander minimum). Pay repeatedly in cycles: Commander family £1 for Commander plus each used surviving officer; other families clockwise £1 per used surviving officer; bank last £1 per used regiment and local-alliance piece. Commander gains one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower/dome (and all matching flags if capital), open all target orders/remove unrest; for new conquest place control token above associated President box, Governor overlay in region and only Governor card in Vacant Offices, unless Governor General is active; move Elephant inside if facing outward. Catastrophe returns Commander’s half trophies rounded up and member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses; Commander has no card to vacate.

evidence.quote: On success, take loot from the bank: £4 per target tower + faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of (surviving officers used in this attempt + 1).

answers.answer: Governor rolls current printed dice pool without penalty, reducing pool by one after every attempt regardless of result. Success takes £1, or £2 if immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one: build ship one stage; commission a regiment to associated President’s Army; or tax £2 unsplit to Company Balance or that President’s treasury. Each successful build is one stage (partial ship in region, then next success completes into associated President’s sea zone). Each tax after first this turn adds unrest. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes holder. Continue with shrinking pool until stop, no dice, or catastrophe.

evidence.quote: Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result.

answers.answer: Company expense is £1 per existing Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army and each ship in sea zones including China; exclude Commanders. If insufficient Balance, take £5 emergency loans; each advances Debt one only while a track space remains, and at max Debt keep taking loans without advancing. Set Balance to zero after loans. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance to expectations for current Standing; if lower, lower Standing one. Then Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1/share to each owner including Chairman; if total paid is strictly greater than expectations, raise Standing one.

evidence.quote: If insufficient, take £5 emergency loans. Each loan advances Debt one only while a track space remains. At maximum Debt, keep taking loans without advancing Debt any further.

answers.answer: For an attack on Company, resolve primary Crisis first, then secondary Rebellions in Bombay→Madras→Bengal Army order; within a Presidency its Commander orders associated regions. Primary ordinary Crisis strength is normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in target; primary Foreign Invasion is ordinary attack die without unrest; each secondary uses only that region’s unrest. Defense: associated Commander chooses/exhausts pieces; if vacant Military Affairs acts; if both vacant Chairman chooses. Exhaust active pieces to at least attack strength, or as many as possible. Local alliance strength usable once and cannot split. Under the summary’s user-approved interpretation, defense total >= attack means attack fails: clear all attacked-region unrest, actual Commander gets one trophy (substitute gains/loses none), and defeated normal primary Invasion removes one attacker tower if possible.

evidence.summary_location: Events — Attacks on Company; Mounting defense
evidence.quote: Attacks in this order: primary Crisis first, then secondary regions in Bombay → Madras → Bengal Army order. Within each Presidency, that Commander chooses the order of its associated regions.

answers.answer: Support −1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM moves proposed policy one space either way and resolves that adjacent policy. Support zero or more passes: law joins passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy then immediate law effects.

evidence.quote: -1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma’s If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM moves proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, before London Season, PM may call special vote if Standing or Debt is on a lined space, and must call if either is starred. Use ordinary support/voting threshold; no policy accompanies it and PM may vote against. Pass: lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, PM takes passed-law token and firms activate. Fail: share scoring value increases by the Court VP token, max ±3 VP/share; PM remains and Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 starts deregulated; 1710 has no deregulation procedures.

evidence.quote: In 1758/Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, PM may call special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt on lined space, and must if either on starred space.

answers.answer: To form a firm, player must manage none; return one eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to invested, flip family board to charter, place a member as first share, set value to leftmost, take £5 from bank into London. Invest with manager consent using same contribution; each contributes £5 from bank to London and creates one share up to ten, but contributions still add £5 beyond cap. Cannot use Chairman share, Company shares if Standing or Debt lined, or shares created this turn even if traded away. Invested workshop never returns to uninvested, gets no bonus/failure VP, and stays invested if firm fails.

evidence.quote: Form a firm — only if you currently manage none: return one eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop to invested side.

answers.answer: Each firm has one attempt/turn and needs at least one ship; strategy may use closed home port but selected port must be open when filled. Secret bids from London; Hobnob has no bid/trade/dividends. At associated Presidency start reveal and roll one die per £1 bid (pay to bank); at least one 1/2 succeeds. Initiative = ships minus successful dice; President’s successful Trade initiative computed likewise. Lowest first; President chooses ties; if President vacant or never trades, firms fill after Commander/Governor opportunities, Chairman breaks ties. Fill open orders up to ships+1 along own route from home; cannot refill own order, may refill Company/other firm orders. Previously filled gives half listed revenue rounded down. Revenue to India; advance value one per full £6 added this turn.

evidence.summary_location: Deregulation — Firm strategies and competing trade
evidence.quote: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Only a firm with at least one ship may select a trade strategy; it may select a closed home port.

answers.answer: Before Company expenses, firms pay in initiative order then others; ties by manager’s most windows, then PM clockwise. Expense £1 per charter ship plus higher of share count or firm value; London and/or India treasuries may pay. If unable, dissolve unless rescued by emergency investment or one-firm emergency merger. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships to shipyards, charter to family side; workshops stay invested. After expenses manager may pay dividends only from India: each dividend £1/share plus £1 manager. Waiver requires both shareholder choice and manager consent. Record total actual cash paid on Balance track; active non-Hobnob paying none records zero; Hobnob keeps old marker. Sweep remaining India money to London.

evidence.summary_location: Deregulation — Firm expenses, rescue and dividends
evidence.quote: Pay £1 per charter ship plus higher of share count or firm value; can use either/both treasuries.

answers.answer: Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. Components generally limited; if supply runs out complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.

evidence.quote: Components are limited: when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible.

answers.answer: Negotiable: enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Not negotiable: officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. For share transfer, return old owner’s family member and replace at share location with member from receiving family; adjust VP when luxury ownership changes. Used/faceup blackmail cannot be traded; blackmail traded must stay facedown.

evidence.quote: May trade: Enterprises; facedown blackmail; family treasury cash; Company/firm shares; promise cards.

answers.answer: Immediate transfers are binding. Future-behavior promises are nonbinding except a printed promise card’s guaranteed effect can be called if possible. Promise calls follow card timing/limits and none during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which. Promise cards may transfer to third party or guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (e.g., workshop paid in Bonuses cannot pay again after sale that phase).

evidence.quote: Immediate transfer — Binding. Promise of future behavior — Nonbinding, except a printed promise card’s guaranteed effect can be called if possible.

answers.answer: Use scenario player setup cards; add three extra cards at five players or six at six players; shuffle/deal evenly. Place every listed holding: cash and enterprises to area, office member and card to holder, Company-share members to Court, writers/officers/trainees to indicated boxes, Commander to Commander slot without office card, ships in listed sea zone or on shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together as one deck; deal three display cards (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown).

evidence.quote: Use that scenario’s player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six players. Shuffle and deal evenly.

answers.answer: Game ends after scenario final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure normally immediate; if during Events finish that phase before Final Scoring; legislation failure finishes the vote before scoring. During all Final Scoring, negotiations and promise calls are prohibited.

evidence.quote: Failure during Events finishes that phase, and legislation failure finishes vote before scoring.

answers.answer: Power counts enterprises and Company shares at current track rates (bottom two spaces zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, +2 PM, and printed card power (blackmail either faceup/down, applicable spouse). Awards by final turn: turns 1–3, 3/1 VP; 4–6, 5/2; 7–8, 8/4. Tied first each get only lower award, no other award; tied second get none. Highest final VP wins; tied final VP breaks by most windows, then clockwise from PM.

evidence.quote: Tied first: only lower award to each tied player; no other award. Tied second receive none.

answers.answer: Final scoring: if Company survived, add current Court VP per Company share; if failed, subtract it per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop (invested workshops excluded). Firm special retirement happens before ordinary scoring either outcome. After Power/Court, survived: roll office attrition then retire Pensioners, no display cards. Failed: instead draw one random Company failure card.

evidence.quote: If Company survived, add Court’s current VP per Company share. If failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP and impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise/share trades happen immediately on taking spouse. Retirement discounts stack, are personal, and each usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring; they reduce actual spending and thus prestige priority.

evidence.quote: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred.

answers.answer: If shipyard returns due to Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship remains in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while the matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.

evidence.quote: Whether a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or an unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play.

answers.answer: Enlist Writer: no cost; place in any Presidency Writers; with ≥4 vacant offices place one extra writer once that turn. Enlist Officer: no cost; place in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury: £4 to bank; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned, window icon, social enterprise. Purchase Shipyard: £2 to bank; place matching ship unfitted on shipyard; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop: £5 to bank; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus, worth 1 VP on Company failure if uninvested. Seek Share: pay bank for empty Exchange space, queue prices £2, £3, £3, £4, £5; applicant, not yet share.

evidence.quote: Purchase Luxury — Pay bank £4; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned, and its window icon; social enterprise.

answers.answer: If a family piece must be placed and supply is empty, take a piece from any own prize and lose its printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

evidence.quote: If placing a family piece with none in supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP.

answers.answer: If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, from a prize (lose prize VP). If impossible, there is no Chairman.

evidence.quote: If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, a prize (lose prize VP).

answers.answer: Director: Chairman chooses current officeholder except Chairman/Governor; if all offices vacant, any writer. Manager of Shipping: Chairman chooses any writer. Military Affairs: Chairman chooses Presidential Commander, otherwise any officer, otherwise trainee. President: Director chooses writer of that Presidency or Governor associated with it. Governor: associated President chooses writer or officer in region; Commander is ineligible. China Superintendent: Chairman chooses any writer and hires immediately on creation. Governor General replaces Director and is hired same way. Ordinary consent rule applies to own-family candidates; Commander appointments exempt; Chairman election Nepotism-exempt.

evidence.quote: Director of Trade: Chairman chooses current officeholder other than Chairman/Governor; if all offices vacant, any writer.

answers.answer: Director may repeatedly make Special Envoy checks, paying £1 treasury per die, no penalty. Success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing Superintendent overlay/card and immediately having Chairman hire a writer. After all Envoys, Director may transfer up to two writers or ships between any Presidencies/sea zones (including China once created). Cannot transfer while still taking Envoys.

evidence.quote: May make repeated Special Envoy checks: £1 treasury cash per die, no penalty.

answers.answer: Military Affairs may make up to two transfers, each one officer or regiment from one Army to another, remaining in top half. Then assign every trainee to any Army top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if vacant or another family has more total pieces in Army than current holder’s family, choose among families with most pieces; move chosen officer to Commander slot and return previous Commander to top as officer. Tie with incumbent does not replace. Nepotism does not apply.

evidence.quote: May make up to two transfers, each officer or regiment from one Army to another, remaining in top half.

answers.answer: Within each Presidency its President chooses order of Commander, Governors and Trade. Commander/Governors may decline; each position finishes before next, Trade cannot interrupt one. If President vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot Trade or approve local-alliance purchases.

evidence.quote: Within EACH Presidency, its President chooses the order of its Commander, Governor(s) and Trade; each position finishes before the next acts.

answers.answer: Trade does not exhaust ships. At Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency Writers box (dividers preserve affiliation); filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply.

evidence.quote: Trade does not exhaust ships.

answers.answer: At start of Commander operations, before Deploy, request President treasury funds for printed-price local alliances; President must approve. Move purchased alliance to top/active. Used for Deploy/defense, exhaust whole piece to bottom; strength usable once and cannot split. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too and does not reactivate them.

evidence.quote: At the START of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts, first request President’s treasury funds for any printed-price local alliances in Army; President must approve purchase.

answers.answer: Against own Company-controlled target, defense penalty is zero. For reopening orders/clearing unrest there are no towers, so zero tower trophies; with no tower or faceup loot modifier use minimum loot equal to surviving participating officers +1 for Commander, distributed normally.

evidence.summary_location: Actions — Deploying in already Company-controlled region
evidence.quote: With no tower or faceup loot modifier, use the minimum loot of surviving participating officers + 1 for the Commander, distributing normally.

answers.answer: Two successful Administer successes total: first places partial ship in Governor’s region if absent; next completes it to associated President’s sea zone. Each success builds one stage. Commissioned regiment goes to Army associated with Governor’s President; officer-like strength, loot paid to bank, no officer-loss rolls.

evidence.quote: Each successful Build performs one stage: if no partial ship is in the Governor’s region, this single success places the partial ship there.

answers.answer: China created by successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case Chairman immediately hires any writer. Treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping/Director may send ships there like any sea zone. China acts after Bengal. China ships count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.

evidence.summary_location: Actions — Superintendent of Trade in China
evidence.quote: Created by successful envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case the Chairman immediately hires any writer.

answers.answer: China may attempt trade only once, even if check fails; one die per ship. Do not attempt without an export icon in Company-controlled regions. On success count export icons in all Company-controlled regions only: Company Balance gets £4 per icon; Superintendent family gets £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company icons do not count; Company revenue is not flat £4.

evidence.quote: After Bengal, may attempt China Trade only ONCE, including a failed attempt: no retry.

answers.answer: When Governor General law creates office, make all Governors pensioners, remove overlays and partial Company ships, return Governor/Director cards to box; replace Director with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue, place ribbon overlay. Thereafter no Governors/overlays on conquest; printed Company symbols indicate control. Skip Governor Elimination when region lost.

evidence.quote: Law creates this office: immediately make all Governors pensioners, remove their overlays and partially built Company ships, return Governor/Director cards to box.

answers.answer: First add £3 Balance per Company region. Govern repeatedly, £1 treasury per die without penalty; every rolled 6 adds unrest to each Company region even on success, and failure adds another unrest to every Company region. Success: Governor General’s family gets £1 per Company region from bank, then must choose one benefit per region: complete ship into any sea zone incl China; regiment into any Army; or £2 to Balance/any office treasury except own, adding unrest to a Company region. If multiple Tax choices, unrest in different regions. Max one successful Govern per turn.

evidence.quote: First Balance +£3 per Company region. Then may attempt Govern repeatedly, paying £1 treasury per die, no penalty.

answers.answer: Only player-owned ships in affected Company fleet zones roll; one roll per eligible ship: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Sunk ships return to shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count Eastern. Firm ships use strategy zone; Hobnob firm ships exempt. Three storms means all sea zones; no storm indication means no checks.

evidence.quote: Company and extra ships — Exempt; never roll storm checks.

answers.answer: When order newly closes, return any writer there to owner’s supply; filled token flips to closed. If told to close in fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected; if connected order already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order instead. If none open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate Cascade once per tile but can receive multiple effects.

evidence.quote: Return any writer on a newly closed order to its owner’s supply; flip a filled token to closed.

answers.answer: Use back of new top tile in draw stack for ordinary top-stack region (not just-drawn tile), unless event specifies. Turmoil closes northernmost open order there; if all closed, Cascade. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders there and all bordering regions. Shuffle: Elephant’s March, shuffle tile into remaining draw stack, separately shuffle discards and place on top; if draw stack empty, March last instead.

evidence.quote: Turmoil: Close northernmost open order in top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade.

answers.answer: Leader: top-stack sovereign region gains a tower. If dominated, it rebels using printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

evidence.quote: Top-stack sovereign region gains one tower. Dominated region instead rebels with printed explosion modifier.

answers.answer: On border, Peace opens orders connected across Elephant’s border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region, then March. If Elephant wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest, then March.

evidence.quote: If Elephant wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March.

answers.answer: Invasion: attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier must be strictly greater than defender’s whole empire strength; equality fails. Success replaces defender flag with attacker’s dominated flag; capturing capital shatters entire empire. If attacker has no empire, use free capital/star plus matching small flag; if none available, no new empire/flags form. Failure costs attacker one tower.

evidence.quote: Sovereign attacker’s whole empire strength + event modifier must be greater than defender’s whole empire strength.

answers.answer: Rebellion compares only rebel region strength + modifier against its sovereign capital strength; other empire regions do not count. Must be strictly greater, so tie fails. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag, closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from capital.

evidence.quote: Must be strictly greater. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed).

answers.answer: Region Loss: Commander returns half family trophies rounded up and member to supply; roll once per associated Army officer, each 6 removes officer. Eliminate Governor: card to unused stack, fatigue/member to supply; remove overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Control token returns to region with £ loot side down, region symbol up. Future conquest has no loot modifier; region loses Presidency association. Invasion closes all orders/Cascades if already closed. Standing loses number of regions lost so far this turn (first −1, second additional −2, etc.). Losing one region does not automatically lose others; resolve their attacks separately.

evidence.quote: Standing loss equals number of regions lost so far this turn, including this one: first -1, second additional -2, etc.

answers.answer: After successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant goes to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise top-stack region. Company region: fully inside. Dominated: point toward sovereign. Sovereign: point across shape-marked border; if neighbor already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not so dominated; if all are, use redirect-arrow border pointing toward empire capital.

evidence.quote: After successful Invasion Crisis, move to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise top-stack region.

answers.answer: Foreign Invasion targets selected by storm die: West Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal, all storms each, none top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. Success closes all orders (Cascade if already all closed), removes target flag and all matching flags if capital, restores dome if Company-controlled, sets tower strength to half attack roll rounded down, then moves Elephant with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. Designer ruling: unrest adds neither attack strength nor resulting towers.

evidence.quote: On success close all orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target’s flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down.

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one law, revealing sequentially. After one or two ordinary draws may stop or continue up to three total; select any revealed law, discard others. A dilemma forces selection of that dilemma and ends drawing. Before voting, PM turns dial clockwise/counterclockwise to first policy space matching chosen law’s bottom icon; that space sets target/consequence. Vote marker starts at law’s printed support.

evidence.quote: After one or two ordinary (non-dilemma) draws, the PM may stop drawing, or continue up to three total.

answers.answer: Tax: each family pays bank £1 per owned target; unpaid target returns to supply (including Chairman if taxed), losing prize/luxury VP. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each prize, returning if unable. Bonus: bank pays each family £1 per owned target. Power: swap target marker with next higher; if already highest, swap any other pair.

evidence.quote: Tax: Each family pays £1 TO THE BANK per target it owns.

answers.answer: Each £1 family cash buys one vote plus printed card votes. Each card may be used only once across all rounds of this vote; rotate when used until resolution. Starting PM clockwise, players cast votes. PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes must end voting.

evidence.quote: Each card’s votes may be used only once in the entire vote, across all rounds: rotate it when used and leave it rotated until vote resolution.

answers.answer: A supporter may later oppose; once opposed cannot support for remainder of vote. Track all opposition votes; largest opponent gets Opposition Leader, ties retain current holder. With recipient consent, votes may be cast for someone already opposed or committing to oppose and add to their opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing except forced use of “Vote with my enterprises” promise.

evidence.quote: A player who voted for may later oppose; once opposed, cannot vote for during this vote.

answers.answer: Final-turn upkeep still occurs. Pay each prize member’s printed upkeep separately; if unpaid, return member and lose prize VP. On nonfinal refresh writers to associated Presidency Writers box; filled tokens/dividers and extra ships to supply; exhausted officers/regiments reactivate; active alliances exhaust and do not reactivate; fitted player ships retain fatigue. Advance turn then begin London Season.

evidence.quote: On final turn, perform upkeep but skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring.

answers.answer: Each shareholder may make one special retirement per London Season from supply, regardless of number of firms. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed highest total dividend marker among firms where they own a share; no retirement from firm whose marker absent/zero. Printed cost may exceed marker if discounts cover difference. Normal retirement and prestige eligibility otherwise apply. At start Final Scoring, firms score then each eligible shareholder gets one special retirement regardless Company outcome, before normal final scoring; no display cards.

evidence.quote: Each shareholder may make one additional retirement per London Season from supply rather than Pensioners, irrespective of number of firms owned.

answers.answer: Firm investments receive £5 from bank into London; trade revenues go to India. London pays ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses; India pays dividends and expenses. Family cash cannot transfer into/out of firm treasuries; only specified procedures move firm money.

evidence.quote: London receives the bank’s £5 per investment and pays for ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses; India receives trade and pays dividends/expenses.

answers.answer: Firms phase is after Family (including Company share creation) and before Hiring. Investments occur without set order until no one wishes more, then strategies are chosen. Manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm; PM resolves conflicts between firms.

evidence.quote: After Family share creation, before Hiring, take investments actions without set order until nobody wishes more. Then choose strategies.

answers.answer: A firm may fit its own or another player’s shipyard ship only with shipyard owner consent; pay £3 from London to bank. May buy player-owned ship already in Company, with owner consent: unfatigued £3 or fatigued £2 paid into Shipping treasury. Cannot acquire Company or extra ships.

evidence.quote: A firm may fit a ship from its own OR ANOTHER PLAYER’S shipyard, but must have that shipyard owner’s consent.

answers.answer: Only a player managing no firm at all may initiate hostile takeover. Obtain consent of holders of majority target shares; move target ships, money and shares to own charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

evidence.quote: Only a player who manages NO firm at all may initiate one; managing a different firm also makes you ineligible.

answers.answer: Merger requires every shareholder’s consent. Highest-value firm is primary; tied highest, players choose. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Share transfers can be negotiated. If primary exceeds ten shares, return excess to owners’ supplies with those owners’ consent. Primary value/dividend tracks remain.

evidence.quote: Managers negotiate with every shareholder’s consent. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied.

answers.answer: Hobnob means no bid, trade or dividends; still pay expenses and retain prior dividend marker for retirement. Hobnob ships are exempt from storms.

evidence.quote: Hobnob — No bid, trade or dividends. Still pay expenses; retain previous dividend marker for retirement.

answers.answer: Yes, at ten-share cap emergency investment still contributes £5 but creates no new share. Emergency investment follows normal Company-share/workshop rules, even beyond cap; pays expenses, loses any remaining cash, and lowers Value one space per emergency investment. Same-turn-created Company shares remain ineligible even if traded away.

evidence.quote: Emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules, even when ten-share cap prevents more shares: pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, lower Value one space per emergency investment.

answers.answer: Emergency negotiated merger is with only one other firm. Normal merger procedure still applies, including consent of every involved shareholder. Other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.

evidence.quote: Alternatively make an emergency negotiated merger with only ONE other firm.

answers.answer: Voluntary dissolution needs consent of all shareholders. Use insolvent-firm dissolution: shares to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return matching shipyards, charter flips to family side. Invested workshops remain invested for rest of game.

evidence.quote: All shareholders must consent. Apply the same dissolution procedure as an insolvent firm.

answers.answer: At Final Scoring, before ordinary Power/Court/outcome scoring, each player adds VP for all shares across all firms then rounds that player’s total down once; subtract 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor’s Prison. Value/share: 1 −1; 2 0; 3–4 ½; 5–7 1; 8–9 1½; 10 2. This firm scoring and special retirement happen whether Company survived or failed.

evidence.summary_location: Scoring — Final Scoring order; firm-track VP
evidence.quote: For each player separately add VP from all their shares across all their firms, then round that player’s total DOWN once.

answers.answer: 1710 turns 1–5, monopoly, no deregulation procedures. 1758 turns 3–7, starts monopoly; may vote deregulation. 1813 turns 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 turns 1–8, same initial position as 1710 with deregulation available.

1710: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, offices £3 each, Royal Protection, one regiment per Army, no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12 expectations, Debt 3, offices £4 each, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship East Indian, Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.

evidence.quote: 1710 | 1–5 | £10 expectations / 0 | £3 | Royal Protection | One regiment per Army; no Company ships.

answers.answer: 1813: turns 5–8; Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, treasuries £3; initial Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens, return Governor General law to box and overlay over Director of Trade; use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors.

evidence.quote: In 1813, put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, return the Governor General law to the box and place its office overlay over Director of Trade.

answers.answer: Power awards: final turns 1–3, first/second 3/1 VP; turns 4–6, 5/2; turns 7–8, 8/4. Tied first players each receive only lower award and no other award; tied second receive none.

evidence.quote: Most/second awards are 3/1 VP if final turn 1–3, 5/2 if turn 4–6, 8/4 if turn 7–8.

answers.answer: Starting Power: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0, Manufacturing 0. Standing expectations spaces £4/6/8/10/12/14/16; S reset above £10. Lined Standing £4/6/8 or Debt 5/6/7/8 permits PM to call vote; starred Standing £4 or Debt 8 requires PM to call.

evidence.quote: Start Power positions: Social 2 power, Company shares 1, Shipping and Manufacturing 0.

answers.answer: No. Foreign Invasion primary attack is ordinary die only, with no unrest added; tower level is ordinary attack die halved down, not modified by unrest. On success close all orders once; if already all closed, Cascade.

evidence.quote: unrest does not add to a Foreign Invasion’s primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels.

answers.answer: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing check to zero dice means failure. Company Fraud at start of Revenue: roll one die per officeholder; reduce Balance by twice highest roll (minimum zero), receive bank cash equal to actual Balance reduction, so no overdraft. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demotes one Commander to officer, then appoints Commander from officers; same former Commander remains eligible.

evidence.quote: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure; Company Fraud is played at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take cash from the bank equal to that actual Balance reduction.

answers.answer: Shared setup: Balance £5; family VP markers zero; local alliances go in named Army boxes; loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose scenario and use setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and political map. Turn marker at scenario date and PM dial arm points to matching date.

evidence.quote: Set Balance to £5, Power tokens on their indicated starting positions, family VP markers to zero, loot tokens money-side up in matching regions.

answers.answer: Order: London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Skip London Season on first turn. Special eligible Deregulation vote is at very start before London Season.

evidence.quote: Each game turn follows: London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh.

answers.answer: Act first with Chairman, or former Chairman if office vacant, then clockwise. Each may retire each Pensioner to a prize; retirement is optional. Pay printed cost; move member to prize and gain printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends for display order, then pay bank. Unused Pensioners do not carry over; return them to supply after display step.

evidence.quote: Starting with the Chairman (former Chairman if vacant), clockwise, each player may retire each pensioner to a prize.

answers.answer: No. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove surviving capital’s starred flag; it is no longer an empire, regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest.

evidence.quote: Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital’s starred flag: it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.

answers.answer: Per share final VP by Value: 1 −1; 2 0; 3 ½; 4 ½; 5 1; 6 1; 7 1; 8 1½; 9 1½; 10 2. Player sums all firm-share values then rounds down once.
Family actions start with Chairman title holder, then clockwise. New Company Shares step begins after all family actions, and resolves applicants if Debt remains.

evidence.quote: Starting with the Chairman title holder, clockwise, each player resolves their family action.

answers.answer: Operation order: Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay → Madras → Bengal → China if created. Skip each vacant office; it takes no action. In each Presidency, its President orders Commander/Governors/Trade.

evidence.quote: Follow the red ribbon left to right: Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay Presidency → Madras Presidency → Bengal Presidency → China Superintendent, if created.

answers.answer: First roll storm die; result identifies affected sea zone, three storms means all zones, no storm indication means no checks; resolve required storms before events. Eligible player-owned ships in Company fleets check; Company/extra exempt; China counts Eastern; firm ships use strategy zone, Hobnob exempt. Die face also sets event count; flip and resolve one tile at a time for that many events. For region, normally use back of new top draw-stack tile, not just-drawn tile, unless event says otherwise.

evidence.quote: Resolve all required storms before drawing any event. Then flip and resolve one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on that die face.

answers.answer: For ordinary Elephant-located Crisis, tail is attacker/acting region and head defender. Sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) means Invasion; dominated actor (small flag or no dome) means Rebellion against sovereign. If Elephant fully inside Company region, Rebellion against Company.

evidence.quote: Its tail is the attacker/acting region; its head is the defender.

answers.answer: Yes. Under the summary’s user-supplied interpretation, compare the total strength of newly exhausted defense pieces with Crisis strength: equal or greater defeats the attack. Exhaust the entire strength-2 alliance piece; its excess is not a failure and the piece cannot be split or reused that turn. Clear all unrest in the attacked region; the actual Commander gains one trophy, while Military Affairs/Chairman substitutes gain or lose none; if this defeats a normal primary Invasion, remove one attacker tower if possible. This is a user-supplied interpretation, not an official ruling. It states the general comparison rule for defense strength, including alliances; the concrete strength-2 versus strength-1 alliance example confirms its application.

evidence.summary_location: Special Rules — user-supplied interpretation; defense table
evidence.quote: An active strength-2 local alliance can successfully defend a strength-1 Crisis by exhausting the whole alliance piece.

answers.answer: Ordinary Crisis is followed by Elephant’s March: after successful Invasion move to successful capital; after other results move to top-stack region. Failed Invasion and both success/failure of Rebellion still march; those outcomes are not exceptions.

evidence.quote: After successful Invasion Crisis, move to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise top-stack region.

answers.answer: Successful non-Company Rebellion makes actor sovereign, removes its flag, and closes all its orders; if all are already closed, Cascade.

evidence.quote: Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed).

answers.answer: Before voting, set Vote marker to the law’s printed starting support value.

evidence.quote: Read law and set Vote marker to its printed starting support.

answers.answer: At start of Revenue before Company, firms pay expenses in initiative order then remaining firms; ties by manager most windows, then PM clockwise. After expenses, managers may pay dividends.

evidence.quote: At start Revenue before Company, firms act in initiative order then other firms; ties by manager’s most windows then PM clockwise order.

answers.answer: Governor General pays £1 from its treasury per die, no penalty. Before checks it adds £3 Company Balance per Company region. After success its family—not Company—gets £1 per Company region from bank.

evidence.quote: Then may attempt Govern repeatedly, paying £1 treasury per die, no penalty.
